name: Yan Xu
bio: Yan Xu works on multimodal AI at Google. He focuses on Gemini post-training for long-context video understanding and on training Gemini as a multimodal judge to guide reinforcement learning for Nano Banana and Gemini Omni.

Previously at Waymo, he worked on perception foundation models and onboard perception systems for autonomous driving. He received his Ph.D. in Electrical and Computer Engineering from Carnegie Mellon University, advised by Kris Kitani, where he studied in-the-wild 3D human pose estimation.

career.title: Software Engineer · Machine Learning
career.description: I work on Gemini post-training for long-context video understanding, evaluation for enterprise customer applications, and multimodal judging for generative models.
career.impact: Our work supports Gemini launches on Google Cloud and provides reward signals for training Nano Banana and Gemini Omni through RL post-training.

career.title: Software Engineer · Machine Learning
career.description: I worked on perception foundation models and Transformer-based onboard detectors, using auto-labeling for iterative data refinement and model training.
career.impact: Our work improved pedestrian and vehicle detection in challenging driving scenarios, including freeway driving, and supported fleet-wide deployment.

career.title: Ph.D. · Computer Vision & Machine Learning
career.description: My Ph.D. research focused on joint 3D human pose estimation and camera calibration, using person re-identification and multi-view geometry.
career.impact: I developed methods that extended multi-person 3D pose estimation to uncalibrated camera networks beyond controlled laboratory settings.

work.title: CamRM: Motion-grounded rating for camera-motion control
